text: Fill in the key morphological descriptors of classic lichen planus.
questions: The classic lichen planus lesion is intensely *pruritic/itchy:One of the classic 'P' features of lichen planus* — itch is a cardinal feature.
The lesions are purple or *violaceous/purple:The characteristic colour of LP lesions* in colour, distinguishing them from the erythematous red of psoriasis.
The borders of lichen planus papules are *polygonal:Describes the angular border shape of the papules*, giving the lesion an angular rather than round outline.
The surface of the papule is planar or *flat-topped/planar:The surface topography that contrasts with dome-shaped papules*, not dome-shaped.
Fine white lacy lines on the surface, called *Wickham striae:Named lacy white lines visible on the lesion surface*, are the diagnostic surface sign of lichen planus.
Lichen planus favours *flexural/flexor:Opposite of the extensor predilection seen in psoriasis* sites such as the wrists and ankles, contrasting with the extensor distribution of psoriasis.
